/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind-ipv6

```[sig-apps] Job should not create pods when created in suspend state ```

I have tested that access from the node is rejected if the nodeIp is _not_ in `loadBalancerSourceRanges`, and that it works if the nodeIP CIDR is in it.

I have not tested with a POD with `hostNetwork:true`, but that should be the same as from a node. To use `hostNetwork:true` makes it possible to write an e2e test for this, but IMO it should not be required in this PR, but perhaps in a separate one.

Here are some iptables dumps for info:
```
# iptables -L
...
Chain OUTPUT (policy ACCEPT)
target     prot opt source               destination         
KUBE-IPVS-OUT-FILTER  all  --  anywhere             anywhere             /* kubernetes ipvs access filter */
KUBE-FIREWALL  all  --  anywhere             anywhere            
...
Chain KUBE-IPVS-OUT-FILTER (1 references)
target     prot opt source               destination         
DROP       all  --  10.0.0.10            anywhere             vaddr 10.0.0.10
# iptables -S
...
-N KUBE-IPVS-OUT-FILTER
...
-A KUBE-IPVS-OUT-FILTER -s 10.0.0.10/32 -m ipvs --vaddr 10.0.0.10 -j DROP
```

Sorry, I was too hasty on the "approve" button. The port must be included. Consider this case:
```yaml
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: alpine2
spec:
  ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack
  selector:
    app: alpine2
  type: LoadBalancer
  allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: false
  ports:
  - port: 8001
    name: nc
```
With loadBalancerIP `10.0.0.10`. The service is accessible from a K8s node on address `10.0.0.10:8001`. But if _another_ service is created:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: alpine1
spec:
  loadBalancerSourceRanges:
  - "192.168.2.0/24"
  - "fd00::c0a8:200/120"
  ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack
  selector:
    app: alpine1
  type: LoadBalancer
  allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: false
  ports:
  - port: 7001
    name: nc
```
And is _also_ assigned the loadBalancerIP `10.0.0.10`, then the first service is not accessible any more from K8s nodes.

This works as expected with `proxy-mode=iptables`, access from nodes still works on the first service even when the second is created with the same loadBalancerIP.

I am not at all sure that this bug is worth solving. Nobody has complained, and the nft proxier is on the way. But if this is not solved, the constraint should be documented with something like:
```
For proxy-mode=ipvs the loadBalancerSourceRanges can't be used to deny access to the service from
K8s nodes or from PODs with "hostNetwork:true".
```
It might be worth introducing a new "ipset". But I don't know...

> It might be worth introducing a new "ipset". But I don't know...

I initially thought of hash:ip,port,ip set only but I was not sure if I could match ipset on ipvs extension parameters.
@uablrek I updated the rule to match on IP + Port + Protocol.

issue_context.title: Can't restrict access from K8s nodes with loadBalancerSourceRanges for proxy-mode=ipvs
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

When using loadBalancerSourceRanges to allow access only from CIDRs outside the cluster segment, access from the K8s nodes (or pods with hostNetwork:true) should be rejected, but for proxy-mode=ipvs it works.

/sig network
/area kube-proxy
/area ipvs

### What did you expect to happen?

Access from K8s nodes should be rejected in the same way as for proxy-mode=iptables

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Define a service with loadBalancerSourceRanges that allows access from a cidr outside the cluster, e.g.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: alpine
spec:
  loadBalancerSourceRanges:
#  - "192.168.1.0/24"
  - "192.168.2.0/24"
#  - "fd00::c0a8:100/120"
  - "fd00::c0a8:200/120"
  ipFamilyPolicy: RequireDualStack
  selector:
    app: alpine
  type: LoadBalancer
  allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: false
  ports:
  - port: 5001
    name: nc
```
The K8s nodes have addresses on 192.168.1.0/24 and fd00::c0a8:100/120.

Make sure a loadBalancerIP is assigned (in this example 10.0.0.0/32) and try to access it from a K8s node:
```
# With proxy.mode=ipvs
> nc 10.0.0.0:5001
alpine-f6c8bd7db-zljnl    # (works)
# With proxy.mode=iptables
# nc 10.0.0.0:5001
# (hangs...)
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Same for both ipv4 and ipv6.

This is related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119524 since a fix requires that the `nodeID` passed to the `kube-proxy` is correct. Please see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119524#issuecomment-1655389139

### Kubernetes version

v1.27.4 and master


### Cloud provider

None

### OS version

Linux 6.4.4

### Install tools

None

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

N/A

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

N/A
comments: @kushalShukla-web Great! But please coordinate with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119524. I hope that one get accepted, and then ~the `nodeIP`s (both families) passed to the proxiers should be usable.~ No, they are not, please see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119656#issuecomment-1664290331

Discussed this one in the SIG Network meeting today: we agree this is something we'd like to implement, however we weren't sure exactly how to do it with ipvs during the meeting. Whoever takes this on needs to come up with and communicate a clear plan of _how_ it will be accomplished.

/triage accepted

@kushalShukla-web My comment https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119656#issuecomment-1655630007 is not feasible. For proxy-mode=ipvs the src and dst is _both_ loadBalancerIP. So the nodeIP will not help :disappointed:

@uablrek I did a small experimented with kind + metallb. 

I created a loadbalancer service backed by [whoami pods](https://github.com/traefik/whoami).

loadBalancerIP: 172.18.255.200
podIP: 10.244.1.3

conntrack picks the src and dst both as loadBalancerIP.
`tcp      6 115 TIME_WAIT src=172.18.255.200 dst=172.18.255.200 sport=44936 dport=80 src=10.244.1.3 dst=10.244.1.1 sport=80 dport=6952 [ASSURED] mark=0 use=1`

Tried to create an iptables rules matching source and destination with loadbalancerIP to drop packets but it didn't work.

After some exploration I found [ipvs match extension for iptables](https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/xenial/man8/iptables-extensions.8.html#:~:text=to%20prot.-,ipvs,-Match%20IPVS%20connection) and with the following rules I was able to prevent access to lbIP from k8s nodes / host network.

```iptables -t filter -A OUTPUT -s 172.18.255.200 -m ipvs --vaddr 172.18.255.200 --vport 80 --vproto tcp -j DROP```

The solution looks hacky though, we only need this rule if source ranges are defined for the service and node ip is not covered by any of them.
Will try to program this in the ipvs proxier.

Good find! :+1:  I had missed the ipvs extension. I started to check nodeIP and the (flawed) `--bind-address` option to experiment with setting a nodeIP as "src" for some routes to dodge the lbip-both-as-src-and-dst problem, and an old "vision" I have to **not** assign clusterIPs to `kube-ipvs0` at all, but have *one* rule to replace them all, like:

```
ip route add local <ClusterIP-CIDR> dev kube-ipvs0 scope host src <node-ip>
```
It *can* be done, and in a cluster with 1000's of clusterIP's it would simplify
